title: Segregated warm-pool controller and surge circuit-breaker
author: Nina Kapoor
release_notes: Adds opt-in per-tenant segregated warm pools for Dedicated and a surge circuit-breaker to prevent noisy-neighbor blast radius; new telemetry metrics and feature flag behind 'segregated_warm_pools_v1'.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated have reported SLA regressions when a single tenant's warm-pool thrash causes sustained headroom depletion across a shared warm pool. This PR introduces two related controls: (1) a segregated warm-pool controller that can allocate warmlets in tenant-scoped pools to limit noisy-neighbor effects, and (2) a surge circuit-breaker that detects rapid utilization spikes across a pool and temporarily gates new reservation commits to protect overall throughput guarantees.

Design summary: segregated warm-pools are configured via the existing FleetConfig API with an optional 'segregation_policy' (none|per-tenant|per-namespace). The controller keeps warm-pool bookkeeping and exposes a small allocator API: AllocateWarmlet(tenant_id, preferred_pool) which prefers tenant pools and falls back to shared pools if disabled. The surge circuit-breaker monitors per-pool short-window utilization (1m/5m) and an estimator for headroom volatility. On breaker trip, the controller emits SurgeBreakerTripped{pool, reason} and enforces a reject-or-defer policy configurable per-fleet. The circuit uses an exponentially decaying trip score to avoid flip-flopping.

Telemetry & observability: new metrics exported via /metrics and console dashboards: redwood_warm_pool_usage_by_pool, redwood_warm_pool_alloc_failures_total, redwood_surgebreaker_state{pool}, redwood_surgebreaker_trips_total, redwood_surgebreaker_backoff_seconds. Added tracing spans for AllocateWarmlet and BreakerEvaluate to make correlation with request traces easier.

Compatibility & rollout: feature gated under 'segregated_warm_pools_v1' feature flag. Default behavior unchanged. Backward-compatible config additions allow tenants to opt into segregation. Documented default thresholds and suggested tuning for small/medium/large fleets in the console docs.

Commits (high-level): 1) 8a3f2b4 - introduce segregated warm-pool controller skeleton + API surface. 2) 2b7d9c1 - wire warm-pool allocator into dedicated reconciler, add unit tests and mocks. 3) d4c11e0 - add surge circuit-breaker logic, telemetry, e2e test harness and docs.

Files/areas changed (high-level): controllers/warmpool_controller.go, controllers/allocator.go, autoscaler/surge_breaker.go, telemetry/metrics_registry.go, console/docs/dedicated-warmpools.md, api/v1/fleet_config.proto, pkg/featureflags/flags.go, internal/tests/e2e/dedicated_surge_test.go, several unit tests and mocks. No schema-breaking RPCs; proto additions are additive.

Testing: unit tests added for allocation fallback logic and breaker hysteresis (coverage + branch checks). Integration e2e harness simulates noisy-tenant load to assert that segregated pools prevent cross-tenant headroom collapse and that the breaker prevents sustained SLA breaches under pathological bursts. CI run initially failed lint due to a formatting regression (fixed in second commit). One intermittent e2e flake in warmlet lifecycle observed in CI; added retry and bolstered assertions to stabilize. All checks green on final run.

Review conversation (summary): - Luca Romano: asked for clearer failure modes when tenant pool is exhausted; requested explicit metrics for allocation rejections. Response: added redwood_warm_pool_alloc_failures_total and a graceful fallback to shared pool when allowed; noted in docs. - Priya Shah: requested tests around breaker decay parameters and an API knob to toggle reject vs defer semantics. Response: added parameter 'surge_policy' to FleetConfig and two additional unit tests to cover both paths. - Diego Morales: requested performance microbenchmark and memory allocation audit for controller caches. Response: added microbench harness results to PR and reduced controller cache retention to avoid long-lived allocations. After addressing comments, reviewers approved.

CI summary: Lint: initially fail (fmt) -> fixed. Unit tests: pass. Integration: pass (one rerun due to flake). Benchmarks: included as artifacts. Coverage: unchanged within tolerance.

Backwards compatibility & migration plan: default off; opt-in migration recommended for fleets with per-tenant SLA issues. If a customer enables per-tenant segregation, warmlets already allocated in a shared pool are gradually drained and re-backed into segregated pools during maintenance windows to avoid instant capacity churn.

Release notes / rollout: ship behind feature flag; enable canary in dedicated-staging, monitor new metrics (surgebreaker_trips_total, warm_pool_alloc_failures). If breaker trips more than 1% of windows for a tenant, recommend tuning thresholds or increasing reserved warmlets for that tenant.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main on 2025-11-13 after approvals.

Follow-ups (next PRs planned): - autoscaler suggestion engine: recommend per-tenant reserve sizing based on historical warmlet churn (ENG-2229). - UI controls in Console to visualize segregated pool allocations and to manually trigger backfills.
